plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do - you can't benefit from bidding higher (you might overpay) or lower (you might lose auctions you'd profit from). Since my value is $20, I should bid exactly $20 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies, since your bid only affects whether you win, not what you pay if you win. Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $29.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, never more than your value. This guarantees non-negative profit whenever you win and avoids overpaying. With a value of $45, I should bid exactly $45 to maximize expected profit, regardless of what Andy and Betty do.
